scenario.name: SANS DFIR & Microsoft Event Log — RDP Lateral Movement, Session Reconnection & BMC Bitmap Cache Forensics
scenario.overview: Picture an active industrial factory floor with a moving assembly conveyor belt, an articulated yellow robotic arm, steel parts bins, and a final quality-seal stamping desk. During the quiet night shift on the factory floor, a saboteur steps beside the moving assembly conveyor right before the automated quality stamp. In this real-world scenario, the intruder moves quietly past the factory quality stamp station into neighboring restricted rooms, then smuggles copied records out past the factory quality stamp station in tiny disguised batches. Only when a quality engineer checks the finished product’s weight and internal wiring against the locked master blueprint cabinet does the factory-line swap appear. In this scenario (T1021.001, SANS DFIR & Microsoft Event Log, RDP Lateral Movement, Session Reconnection & BMC Bitmap Cache Forensics), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: outbound mstsc.exe Connection, MRU Registry, then destination Server NLA Logon , RdpCoreTS 131, then client-Side RDP Bitmap Cache Visual Screen. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Outbound mstsc.exe Connection, MRU Registry, then Destination Server NLA Logon , RdpCoreTS 131, then Client-Side RDP Bitmap Cache Visual Screen, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 11 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.subtitle: Lateral Movement (T1021.001 - Remote Services: Remote Desktop Protocol)
stages.description: During the quiet night shift on the factory floor, a saboteur steps beside the moving assembly conveyor right before the automated quality stamp. Specifically in Step 1, the intruder moves quietly past the factory quality stamp station into neighboring restricted rooms while everyday visitors and the factory quality inspector go about their routine. When the attacker launches mstsc.exe on source host WKS-07 (10.10.4.19) to connect to SRV-APP02 (10.10.20.45), Windows records the target IP/hostname in NTUSER.DAT (Software\Microsoft\Terminal Server Client\Servers\10.10.20.45\UsernameHint) and logs EventID 1024 (RDP ClientActiveX is trying to connect) and EventID 1102 in Microsoft-Windows-TerminalServices-RDPClient/Operational (logged in WinEvent Event 1024 with SourceHost=WKS-07.corp.local , 10.10.4.19, LogChannel=Microsoft-Windows-TerminalServices-RDPClient/Operational, EventID=1024 , Connection Attempt / 1102 , Server IP, RegistryMru=Software\Microsoft\Terminal Server Client\Servers\10.10.20.45 so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Next, the follow-up artifact Registry Artifact: NTUSER.DAT\Software\Microsoft\Terminal Server Client\Servers\10.10.20.45 (UsernameHint + CertHash) runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , Registry Artifact: NTUSER.DAT\Software\Microsoft\Terminal Server Client\Servers\10.10.20.45 so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1021.001 during "Outbound mstsc.exe Connection, MRU Registry & RDPClient EventID 1024 / 1102 on Source Host" , When the attacker launches mstsc while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). stages.subtitle: Lateral Movement (T1021.001 - Destination LSM EventID 21/24/25 & RdpCoreTS 131)
stages.description: The robotic arm pauses for a heartbeat as the saboteur swaps one genuine component on the belt for an identical-looking counterfeit part carrying a hidden wire. Here in Step 2 inside the factory floor, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the factory quality stamp station in tiny disguised batches without disturbing the original master blueprint cabinet. On destination server SRV-APP02, Microsoft-Windows-RemoteDesktopServices-RdpCoreTS/Operational logs EventID 131 (Client IP:Port 10.10.4.19:54912), Security logs EventID 4624 (LogonType 10 RemoteInteractive or LogonType 7 when reconnecting to a locked session), and TerminalServices-LocalSessionManager/Operational logs EventID 21 (Session logon succeeded, Session ID 2) or EventID 25 (Session reconnection succeeded) (logged in WinEvent Event 21 with LogChannel=TerminalServices-LocalSessionManager/Operational, EventID=21 , Session Logon / 25 , Session Reconnect / 24 , Disconnect, SessionId=2, SourceNetworkAddress=10.10.4.19 so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Next, the follow-up artifact Security EventID 4624: LogonType=10 (RemoteInteractive) IpAddress=10.10.4.19 runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , Security EventID 4624: LogonType=10 , RemoteInteractive IpAddress=10.10.4.19 via System / Ru so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1021.001 during "Destination Server NLA Logon , EventID 4624 Type 10 / 7, RdpCoreTS 131 & LSM EventID 21 / 25" , On destination server SRV-APP02, Microsoft-Windows-RemoteDesktopServices-RdpCoreTS/Operational logs EventID 131 , Client IP:Port 10 while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ svchost.exe -k NetworkService -s TermService (Session 2 Logon from 10.10.4.19) / ⇠#2 ACK 21) from Node ② (#2 Core Identity & VLAN Switch) to Node ③ (#3 Internal VLAN Router (:3389)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 BMC Cache & Default.rdp Registry).

stages.title: Stage 3: Client-Side RDP Bitmap Cache (Cache0000.bin / bmc2-tools) Visual Screen Reconstruction
stages.subtitle: Collection (T1021.001 - RDP Bitmap Cache Visual Reconstruction)
stages.description: The assembly line rolls forward, the factory press stamps the official warranty seal right onto the tampered unit, and trucks ship it to every trusting customer. In this final step inside the factory floor, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the factory quality stamp station in tiny disguised batches until the assembly line inspection camera catches the mismatch. During the interactive session on SRV-APP02, mstsc.exe on WKS-07 caches 64x64 pixel screen tiles inside %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Terminal Server Client\Cache\Cache0000.bin (and bcache24.bmc). Using ANSSI bmc-tools and Rdpieces, DFIR analysts carve and reassemble the bitmap tiles from WKS-07 to visually reconstruct the exact GUI tools and commands the attacker ran on SRV-APP02 (logged in Sysmon Event 11 with ArtifactFile=%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Terminal Server Client\Cache\Cache0000.bin, TileDimensions=64x64 Raw Bitmap Tiles, ForensicParser=ANSSI bmc-tools.py + Rdpieces, EvidentiaryValue=Visual reconstruction of attacker GUI actions on remote host so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes Artifact Path: C:\Users\admin_db\AppData\Local\Microsoft\Terminal Server Client\Cache\Cache0000.bin (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , Artifact Path: C:\Users\admin_db\AppData\Local\Microsoft\Terminal Server Client\Cache\Cache0 so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1021.001 during "Client-Side RDP Bitmap Cache , Cache0000.bin / bmc2-tools Visual Screen Reconstruction" , During the interactive session on SRV-APP02, mstsc while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact python3 bmc-tools.py -s Cache0000.bin -d ./extracted_tiles -b runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , python3 bmc-tools.py -s Cache0000.bin -d ./extracted_tiles -b via python3, passing the exact so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1021.001 during "Client-Side RDP Bitmap Cache , Cache0000.bin / bmc2-tools Visual Screen Reconstruction" , During the interactive session on SRV-APP02, mstsc while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ mstsc.exe writing 64x64 RDP bitmap tiles to Cache0000.bin / ⇠#3 ACK 11) from Node ③ (#3 Internal VLAN Router (:3389)) to Node ④ (#4 Target Server SRV-APP02 (TermService)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 BMC Cache & Default.rdp Registry).
